trial_court: Family Court, Mandla, Civil Suit No.1-A/2014
case_name: Rajesh Kumar Gupta vs Smt. Mohani Gupta
facts_of_case: Appellant/husband married respondent/wife in 2008 and they had a son in 2011. Husband filed divorce petition in 2012 alleging wife's unnatural behavior and mental condition was not sound & proper.

legal_principles.principle: A party is impotent if his or her mental or physical condition makes consummation of the marriage a practical impossibility.
legal_principles.held: The condition must be one, according to the statute, which existed at the time of the marriage and continued to be so until the institution of the proceedings.
cited_cases: Digvijay Sinhji v. Pratap Kumari, (1969) 2 SCC 279 : AIR 1970 SC 137

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty for the purposes of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 will not depend upon the numerical count of such incidents or only on the continuous course of such conduct but really go by the intensity, gravity and stigmatic impact of it when meted out even once.
legal_principles.held: The intensity, gravity and stigmatic impact of it when meted out even once and the deleterious effect of it on the mental attitude, necessary for maintaining a conducive matrimonial home.
cited_cases: Rajani v. Subramonian, AIR 1990 Ker 1 : (1990) 1 DMC 561

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree dated 5.4.2014 were upheld, dismissing the husband's petition for grant of divorce.
